description:
Follow-up to fz-qe0, which removed the dominant term (the recursive-group
reachability walk stepping into settled products: 21.9M node visits -> 9.9K,
run 12.2s -> 3.9s).

The fixture is still ~3.15s debug on a fast dev machine, which by
[[feedback_tiny_fixture_slowness_is_correctness]] is still excess work for a
24-line program: a tiny fixture measured in seconds means repeated work, not hard
work.

## Measured (fz-qe0 HEAD, --log-telemetry, interp lane)

Time attributed to the gap preceding each product settle:

    executable_facts          533 settles    429 ms
    runtime_demand              3 settles    343 ms
    callable_construction    2625 settles    229 ms   (was 6704 ms)
    transport_shape          2702 settles    159 ms
    abi_executable            242 settles     65 ms

plus ~0.9s inside drive jobs, of which AnalyzeActivation is 921 spans / 791 ms.

## THE SIGNAL IS THE COUNT, NOT THE COST

242 executables but 2625 callable_construction and 2702 transport_shape
settlements -- about 11 of each per executable. Each is now cheap, so the wall
clock no longer screams, but the POPULATION is the thing to explain: either those
are genuinely distinct positions, or products are re-settling (churn). Establish
which BEFORE optimizing anything -- if it is churn it belongs to the
fz-go4.18.28 transport-monolith / partial-publication family and the fix is
upstream.

921 AnalyzeActivation spans for this fixture is also worth a census against the
activation inventory.

FIRST STEP: count DISTINCT ProductKeys settled per kind versus total settlements.
Equal => genuine population, look at why position count is 11x executable count.
Unequal => churn, and the re-settle triggers are the lead.

## Re-measure first: the input may have shrunk

fz-6gb landed after these numbers were taken and cut executable fanout ~5x on
lambda-heavy programs (32 distinct lambdas: 233 executables -> 45). This fixture
has 24 lambda call sites, so its 242 executables and the per-executable ratios
above may be materially different now. Re-run the telemetry census before
drawing conclusions from the table.

## The budget is no longer the detector

The fixture's `timeout.run_secs` / `timeout.interp_secs` were 6s specifically to
keep this visible. That did not survive contact with CI -- a wall-clock budget
calibrated on dev hardware exceeded its cap on EVERY CI run of the
fz-go4.1..fz-f98.24 stack, because the runners are slower and run under
`llvm-cov` instrumentation. The caps are now 20s hang backstops, documented as
deliberately too loose to notice a regression (main 120c86192).

So DO NOT rely on the fixture budget to catch a regression here, and do not
tighten it again -- that was tried and it produced a permanently red CI signal
that everyone learned to ignore. The replacement detector is a machine
independent work-count ceiling asserting the settlement volume above:
fz-f98.23.

comments.text:
SUPERSEDED IN PART by fz-zg4 (PR #92, commit 7071dbe24). Read that first -- it has the instrument this ticket asked for.

fz-xat asked: are the 2625 callable_construction settlements for 242 executables genuine population or churn? FIRST STEP was 'count DISTINCT ProductKeys settled per kind versus total settlements'. That question is now partly answered from a different direction, and the answer moved the focus.

MEASURED on a ladder of n identical Enum.find call sites (complexity strictly linear, so anything that is not linear is structural):

  kind                    settles n=1 -> n=32     us/settle n=1 -> n=32
  runtime_demand          3 -> 3                  2145 -> 116681   (54x)
  root_backend_product    3 -> 3                  75 -> 1905       (25x)
  incoming_input_relations 1 -> 34                78 -> 1670       (21x)
  transport_shape         180 -> 3001             43 -> 74
  callable_construction   171 -> 2900             60 -> 90
  executable_facts        31 -> 292               65 -> 64   FLAT
  abi_executable          16 -> 233               263 -> 273 FLAT

THE POPULATION IS FINE. transport_shape and callable_construction settle counts track the executable count (~13 per executable at both ends of the ladder) and their per-settle cost is near-flat. That is the incremental shape: count grows with the program, cost per unit does not. So the 2625 settlements are population, NOT churn -- this ticket's headline suspicion does not survive the measurement.

THE REAL SHAPE is the opposite: kinds whose settle count is CONSTANT while per-settle cost grows. runtime_demand settles 3 times regardless of program size and absorbs the whole program each time (231 of 233 executables in one cone, external_members = 0 at every size). That is a pass wearing a product's clothes, and it is now fz-zg4.

STILL OPEN HERE, genuinely: enum_predicate_search remains ~2.6s interp / ~3.1s run against its 6s pins. runtime_demand is ~350ms of it and belongs to fz-zg4. AnalyzeActivation is 921 spans / 791 ms and is NOT explained by anything above -- that is the part of fz-xat worth keeping. Suggest re-scoping this ticket to the AnalyzeActivation census (921 spans for this fixture, against the activation inventory: population or repeat?), and letting fz-zg4 own the demand cone.

Tooling note: .agent/docs/performance-instrumentation.md (added in fz-zg4) documents how the numbers above were taken, including the ladder technique and the counts-vs-per-unit-cost reading.

CI EVIDENCE, and the tripwire that was supposed to catch this has been retired.

This fixture's ~3s compile has been blowing its wall-clock cap on EVERY CI run of
the fz-go4.1..fz-f98.19 stack -- PRs #80, #90, #91, #92 and #99 -- as

    ---- matrix::enum_predicate_search::run ----
    fz2 exceeded 6s; stderr:

It went unnoticed because from #93 to #98 the lib suite failed first and cargo's
fail-fast meant the matrix never ran. fz-f98.19 made the lib suite green, the
matrix ran again, and the long-standing failure surfaced.

Measured, debug build, fast dev machine:

    enum_predicate_search   3.15s   cap 6s    CI: FAILED
    enum_take_drop_split    6.1s    cap 15s   CI: passed

So CI needs more than ~2x the local time even for the fixture that passes. The
caps are now 15s on both, documented in the fixture header as HANG BACKSTOPS
that are deliberately too loose to notice a perf regression, and the perf gate
moves to a work-count ceiling in fz-f98.23 (which cites this ticket's 2625
callable_construction settlements for 242 executables as the number to assert).

Nothing here changes the underlying finding: 3.15s to compile a 24-line program
is excess work, and by [[feedback_tiny_fixture_slowness_is_correctness]] that is
a correctness signal. This ticket is still the fix. What changed is that its
detector is no longer a stopwatch calibrated on one machine.

title: enum_predicate_search still compiles for ~3s after the settled-product pruning: 2625 callable_construction settlements for 242 executables
